name: Unilateral Declaration of Egyptian Independence
summary: The Unilateral Declaration of Egyptian Independence by the United Kingdom ends its protectorate over Egypt, and grants the country nominal independence, reserving control of military and diplomatic matters. The Unilateral Declaration of Egyptian Independence on 28 February 1922 was the formal legal instrument by which the United Kingdom recognised Egypt as an independent sovereign state.

name: Genoa Conference
summary: Genoa Conference: The representatives of 34 countries convene to speak in Genoa, Italy about monetary economics, in the wake of World War I. The event affected the balance of power and shaped subsequent military or political decisions, while its consequences extended beyond the immediate confrontation. It became part of the wider struggle that defined the period.

name: League of Nations mandate
summary: The German protectorate of Togoland is divided into the League of Nations mandates of French Togoland and British Togoland. A League of Nations mandate represented a legal status under international law for specific territories following World War I, involving the transfer of control from one nation to another. These mandates served as legal documents establishing the internationally agreed terms for administering the territory on behalf of the League of Nations.

name: League of Nations
summary: The Mandate of Palestine is approved by the Council of the League of Nations. The League of Nations (LN or LoN; French: Société des Nations [sɔsjete de nɑsjɔ̃], SdN) was the first worldwide intergovernmental organisation whose principal mission was to maintain world peace. It was founded on 10 January 1920 by the Paris Peace Conference that ended the First World War.

name: 11 September 1922 Revolution
summary: September 24 (O.S. September 11) – 11 September 1922 Revolution in Greece. The 11 September 1922 Revolution (Greek: Επανάσταση της 11ης Σεπτεμβρίου 1922) was an uprising by the Greek Army and Navy against the government in Athens, which installed a "Revolutionary Committee" in its place. The uprising took place on 24 September 1922, although the date was "11 September" on the Julian calendar still in use at the time in Greece.

name: Second World War
summary: In Italy, the March on Rome brings the National Fascist Party and Benito Mussolini to power. Italy begins a period of dictatorship that lasts until the end of the Second World War. The event affected the balance of power and shaped subsequent military or political decisions, while its consequences extended beyond the immediate confrontation. It became part of the wider struggle that defined the period.

name: Sigma Gamma Rho
summary: Sigma Gamma Rho (ΣΓΡ) Sorority, Incorporated is founded by seven educators in Indianapolis, Indiana. The group becomes an incorporated national collegiate sorority on December 30, 1929, when a charter is granted to the Alpha chapter at Butler University in Indianapolis. Sigma Gamma Rho Sorority, Inc. (ΣΓΡ) is a historically African American sorority.

name: In the 1922 United Kingdom general election forced by the Conservatives'...
summary: In the 1922 United Kingdom general election forced by the Conservatives' withdrawal from the coalition government, the Conservative Party wins an overall majority. Labour for the first time becomes the main opposition party, winning more seats than the divided Liberals. A dining club of newly elected Conservative Members of Parliament evolves the following year into the 1922 Committee.

name: Rebecca Felton
summary: Rebecca Felton of Georgia takes the oath of office, formally becoming the first woman United States Senator. The development drew international attention and influenced later political, social, or strategic decisions connected to the period. Its consequences helped shape how governments and the public understood the wider changes underway.

summary: Kurd Istigdul Djemijetin, the Kurdish Independence Committee, is founded.
